label: rem:nuclear-regimes-shadow-price-kinks-prior-art
title: Prior art for toric chamber flips, magic-shell shadow-price kinks, and finite-nucleon phase walls
html:
The regime transitions in Three operator regimes for nuclear binding and the integer cluster assembly in Physical cluster chamber, drip-line monomer reduction, and the Hoyle triple-alpha bottleneck realize a sharp geometric mechanism that connects combinatorial optimization, density-functional theory, and nuclear shell physics.

Two-layer Gröbner architecture: microscopic \mathrm{HeckeGS} versus macroscopic \mathrm{ChamberGS}

Nuclear assembly separates into two distinct reduction layers:

  1. Layer 1 (\mathrm{HeckeGS} --- noncommutative braid reduction). Confluent Gröbner--Shirshov reduction in H_n(q) \twoheadrightarrow TL_n(q), following Leonid A. Bokut [bokut2001] and Seok-Jin Kang, Kyu-Hwan Lee, Kyungyong Lee, and Hee Oh [kangleeleeoh2002], evaluates the exact rational trace polynomials of elementary colour-singlet motifs as functions of q.
  2. Layer 2 (\mathrm{ChamberGS} --- commutative toric reduction over motifs and capacitated shells). Assembling (Z, N) from integer motif and Mayer--Jensen shell-slack counts u \in \mathbb{N}^m under A u = b(Z, N) is a parametric integer program in the sense of Jack E. Graver [graver1975], Pasqualina Conti and Carlo Traverso [conti-traverso1991], and Bernd Sturmfels and Rekha R. Thomas [sturmfels-thomas1997], dual to the regular-triangulation and secondary-polytope flips of Louis J. Billera, Israel M. Gel'fand, and Bernd Sturmfels [billera-gelfand-sturmfels1990]. Working directly over \mathbb{N}^m via finite Graver and reduced Gröbner test sets automatically produces integer remainder monomers---accounting for odd--even pairing staggering without fractional half-\alpha continuous relaxation artifacts---and unites regime switches, magic-shell closures (w_s = 0), and \alpha-emission walls (x_{\mathrm{par}} \to x_{\mathrm{dau}} x_\alpha) as Gröbner flips across chamber facets, while relegating interior-point solvers to offline discovery oracles.

Finite-nucleon kinks without a thermodynamic limit

In canonical statistical mechanics at positive temperature, Tsung-Dao Lee and Chen-Ning Yang [lee-yang1952] proved that a finite sum of positive analytic Boltzmann weights is smooth, so non-analytic phase boundaries arise only as partition-function zeros pinch the real axis in the thermodynamic limit N \to \infty. Ground-state variational minimization over a finite motif set F or a finite-dimensional Wedderburn spectrahedron obeys the opposite geometry---the zero-temperature Maslov dequantization limit developed in tropical geometry by Oleg Viro [viro2001]. For any finite nonempty family F over an ordered field, the envelope E(\theta) = \min_{i \in F}(a_i + b_i \theta) is concave and piecewise-linear. At any chamber wall \theta^* where the active minimizer switches from branch i of slope b_i to branch j of strictly smaller slope b_j < b_i, the left and right chemical potentials jump discontinuously by b_i - b_j > 0 at finite |F|, producing exact kinks at finite nucleon numbers (A = 4, 16, 40, \dots and coordination k = 12) with no N \to \infty limit.

Magic-shell closures as normal-cone shadow-price jumps

In the dual program, these finite-A vertices correspond to multi-dimensional normal cones where the dual shadow prices u_\lambda^- and u_\lambda^+ on either side of a shell closure cease to agree. Maria Goeppert Mayer [mayer1949] and Otto Haxel, J. Hans D. Jensen, and Hans E. Suess [haxel-jensen-suess1949] identified the nuclear magic numbers \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} empirically through abrupt drops in nucleon separation energies across closed spin--orbit shells. In many-body ground-state theory, John P. Perdew, Robert G. Parr, Mel Levy, and Jose L. Balduz Jr. [perdew-parr-levy-balduz1982] established piecewise linearity of E(N) between integer particle numbers together with exact derivative discontinuities (chemical-potential jumps) at closed shells, while Brecht Verstichel, Helen van Aggelen, Dimitri Van Neck, Paul W. Ayers, and Patrick Bultinck [verstichel-vanaggelen2009] and Valentin Zauner, David Draxler, Laurens Vanderstraeten, Jutho Haegeman, and Frank Verstraete [zauner-verstraete2016] showed that first-order transitions and shell kinks correspond respectively to flat exposed facets and non-smooth vertices of the reduced-density-matrix spectrahedron.
